classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange and factor using common factors, grouping and a quadratic in x², then sketch and read sign intervals while handling repeated roots and endpoint inclusion.

content.prompt: Solve these polynomial inequalities. Start by moving all terms to the LHS.

spec.description: Blank Cartesian axes with arrowheads at both ends; no ticks, grid or origin label.
spec.answerVisibility: Axes remain visible; the curve and intercept values appear only in the solution.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^3-4x&>0\\x(x-2)(x+2)&>0\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x(x-2)(x+2)$. Its $x$-intercepts are $-2,0,2$, and its right-hand end rises. The graph is above the $x$-axis for $-2<x<0$ or $x>2$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^3-5x^2&<0\\x^2(x-5)&<0\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x^2(x-5)$. The graph touches the $x$-axis at $x=0$ and crosses at $x=5$. It lies below the axis for $x<5$, except at $x=0$. Hence $x<5$, $x\ne0$.

spec.description: Solution graph touching at zero and crossing at five.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2(x-5); zero is a double root.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^3-4x^2+4x&\le0\\x(x-2)^2&\le0\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x(x-2)^2$. The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=0$ and touches it at $x=2$. It is on or below the axis when $x\le0$ or $x=2$.

spec.description: Solution sketch crossing at zero and touching at two.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^3-6x^2+x-6&\ge0\\x^2(x-6)+(x-6)&\ge0\\(x-6)(x^2+1)&\ge0\end{align*}$$
Since $x^2+1>0$, the graph of $y=(x-6)(x^2+1)$ has its only $x$-intercept at $x=6$. It is on or above the $x$-axis for $x\ge6$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x^3-6x^2-4x+12&<0\\2x^2(x-3)-4(x-3)&<0\\2(x-3)(x^2-2)&<0\\2(x-3)(x-\sqrt2)(x+\sqrt2)&<0\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=2(x-3)(x^2-2)$. The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $-\sqrt2,\sqrt2,3$, and its right-hand end rises. It is below the axis for $x<-\sqrt2$ or $\sqrt2<x<3$.
